prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (ideology-free; no parties or individuals named)

Economy and public finances
- Eliminate most of the structural deficit within a Parliament; create an independent fiscal watchdog; deliver an emergency budget; cut wasteful spending and some quangos; one-year public sector pay freeze (excluding the lowest paid); review bringing forward the state pension age to 66; cap very high public pensions; cut ministers’ pay; reduce the number of MPs.
- Cancel most of the planned rise in employer/employee National Insurance for lower and middle earners, funded by efficiency savings.
- Improve tax competitiveness and simplicity: cut corporation tax rates (funded by relief simplification), publish a five‑year corporate tax roadmap, create an Office of Tax Simplification, and make the UK more attractive for multinationals and intellectual property.
- Promote saving: restore the earnings link for the basic state pension; support auto‑enrolment; end the effective obligation to buy an annuity at 75.
- Consumer finance: establish a consumer protection body, clearer card terms, cooling‑off for store cards, free national financial advice, and protections against forced home sales for small unsecured debts.

Jobs, welfare, skills and enterprise
- Replace existing schemes with a single Work Programme, reassess incapacity benefits, pay providers by results, require work for long‑term claimants, and apply sanctions for refusals.
- Support start‑ups and SMEs: temporary employer NI holiday for new firms’ first hires; automatic small business rate relief; target 25% of government procurement to SMEs; mentoring and loans for self‑employment; keep the minimum wage; enforce equal‑pay audits on discriminators.
- Create 400,000 training, apprenticeship and college places over two years; bonuses for SME apprentices; all‑age careers service; free colleges from central control; expand alternative routes into teaching; raise entry standards; strengthen discipline powers.

Infrastructure and regional growth
- High‑speed rail linking major cities; oppose additional runways at key airports while improving surface links; reform rail franchising and passenger advocacy; support electrification and Crossrail; expand EV charging; consider a fair fuel stabiliser.
- Nationwide superfast broadband via infrastructure sharing; possible use of licence‑fee funds; replace regional development agencies with local enterprise partnerships; allow councils to benefit from business‑rate growth and offer local discounts.

Public services and health
- Publish granular spending and salaries; encourage employee‑led mutuals; expand payment by results.
- NHS: real‑terms funding increases; patient choice of any qualified provider at NHS prices; GP‑led commissioning; reduce non‑clinical targets and admin costs; 24/7 urgent care access; halt forced A&E/maternity closures; expand single rooms; cancer drugs fund; new dentistry contract; combined personal health/social care budgets; voluntary insurance option to protect homes from care costs; stronger public health with targeted funding.

Education
- More rigorous curriculum and exams (including phonics and a reading check at age six); technical academies; reform league tables; allow high‑quality new schools and expand academy status (including primaries); pupil premium for disadvantaged pupils; protect special schools; tougher Ofsted for weak schools.

Crime, policing and borders
- Tighten alcohol licensing and pricing abuses; early‑intervention sanctions; tougher knife crime sentencing; better victim information.
- Cut police paperwork; restore professional discretion; publish neighbourhood crime data; directly elected local policing leaders; create a Border Police Force.
- Prisons focused on rehabilitation with payment by results; abstinence‑based drug orders; temporary bans on new “legal highs.”

Political and constitutional reform
- Recall for MPs guilty of serious wrongdoing; cap large donations; tighten lobbying rules; equalise constituency sizes; individual voter registration; strengthen parliament’s control of its business; expand open data; publish contracts; reduce quangos.
- Devolve power: local referendums, veto excessive council tax rises, community rights to buy/run services, general power of competence for councils, elected city mayors.
- Civil liberties: scrap ID cards and major databases; UK‑specific bill of rights; curb disproportionate surveillance; limit DNA retention; scale back vetting/barring.

Devolution and the Union
- Implement Scottish fiscal and accountability changes; allow a Welsh powers referendum; support Northern Ireland institutions; address voting on England‑only laws.

Environment and energy
- Green Investment Bank; carbon price floor; “Green Deal” home efficiency; smart grid/meters; emissions performance standard; new nuclear (no subsidy); four CCS plants; offshore grid; community incentives for renewables; diversify gas supply and expand storage.
- Biodiversity and countryside protections; reform CAP/CFP; high animal‑welfare standards; marine conservation zones; anti‑illegal logging; tree planting; pay‑to‑recycle incentives; water market reforms; stronger flood resilience.

Foreign policy, defence and development
- National Security Council; strategic defence review; reform procurement; maintain the nuclear deterrent; support operations in Afghanistan; strengthen support for service personnel and families; act against extremist groups.
- EU: require referendums for future power transfers; sovereignty legislation; seek return of specific powers; no Euro entry.
- Aid: legislate to reach 0.7% of national income by 2013; rigorous transparency and results‑based funding; focus on basics (water, health, education), women/children/disabled; at least £500m annually to tackle malaria; prioritise trade, property rights and rule of law; climate‑smart aid and green export support.
